title: Chapter 20: The Sunny Pair 2
content:
Chapter 20

The Sunny Pair 2

When prominent clan leaders head out for a night-hunt, they usually travel with a massive entourage—all flags flying and retinues trailing behind. Lan Wangji, on the other hand, had always been a lone wolf. Besides, with a severed arm this sinister and unpredictable, a single misstep could get bystanders killed. So he left the disciples and inner-circle cultivators behind, bringing along only Wei Wuxian—and keeping an eagle eye on him the entire way.

Wei Wuxian’s initial game plan had been to find an opening during the descent and vanish into thin air. But after several botched escape attempts, every single bid ended with him dangling by the scruff of his collar from Lan Wangji’s fist.

Changing tactics, he switched to playing the cloying, shameless pest. He latched onto Lan Wangji at every opportunity, and when night fell, he made a point of crawling into Lan Wangji’s bedroll like clockwork, praying the man would be so thoroughly repulsed he’d finally draw his sword and banish him.

Yet no matter how wildly Wei Wuxian threw himself at him, Lan Wangji remained as unyielding as a boulder. The instant Wei Wuxian wriggled under his blanket, Lan Wangji would drop a soft palm strike that instantly paralyzed him, tuck him into a separate bedroll, and leave him pinned flat in a model sleeping posture until daybreak.

After waking up stiff, sore, and full of regrets for the umpteenth time, Wei Wuxian couldn't help brooding: Growing up really ruined him. Where did the fun go? Teasing him used to be a riot—at least back then his ears would burn! Now he’s not just an unshakeable wall; he’s learned how to counter-attack. Completely unreasonable!

Following the severed left hand’s lead, the two traveled northwest, harmonizing a daily rendition of Rest to temporarily suppress its boiling wrath and bloodlust. By the time they reached the borders of Qinghe, the limb's days-long pointing suddenly shifted: the extended index finger curled inward, balling all five digits into a tight fist.

Whatever it was hunting was right in the area.

Inquiring as they walked, they soon arrived in a lively border town in Qinghe. The midday sun was high, and the bustling main thoroughfare was alive with foot traffic. Wei Wuxian was shuffling along in Lan Wangji’s wake when an aggressively pungent floral stench hit him square in the face.

Used to the crisp, clean scent of Lan Wangji’s cold sandalwood, the greasy floral perfume made his nose twitch. "What kind of scent are you peddling? It's practically peeling the paint off the walls."

The offending odor belonged to an itinerant quack clad in loose Taoist robes, with a face practically stamped with the words Confidence Trickster. He had a wooden vendor's chest slung over one shoulder, hawking cheap odds and ends to the crowd. Delighted to catch a customer, his face split into a grin. "A little bit of everything, young master! Top-shelf cosmetics and scented powders at bottom-shelf prices. Care to take a look?"

"Sure," Wei Wuxian humored him. "Let's see what you've got."

The vendor leaned in. "Looking for a gift for the lady of the house?"

Wei Wuxian flashed an easy grin. "Nope. It's for me."

The peddler’s smile froze solid. Is this clown pulling my leg?!

Before he could snap, another young man stepped up, his expression carved from stone. "If you aren't buying, don't stir up trouble."

The newcomer was breathtakingly handsome, clad in snow-white robes with a matching forehead ribbon, light amber eyes cool as glass, and an elegant spiritual blade slung at his hip. As a faux-priest, the vendor might not know the intricate politics of the cultivation world, but he certainly recognized the sacred cloud motif of the Gusu Lan Clan. Not daring to test his luck, he hoisted his chest strap and scurried away.

Wei Wuxian called after him, "Hey, what are you running for? I was actually going to buy!"

Lan Wangji looked down at him. "Do you have the coin?"

"If I don't, you can pay for me," Wei Wuxian fired back, casually slipping a hand into Lan Wangji’s breast lapel. He hadn't actually expected to find anything, but after a quick pat down, his fingers closed around a dainty, surprisingly heavy silk pouch.

Carrying cash was entirely out of character for Lan Wangji, but over the past few days, the man had shattered so many expectations that Wei Wuxian barely batted an eye. Pocketing the coin pouch, he turned and strolled off. Lan Wangji let him take it, let him walk, and didn't utter a peep of protest.

If Wei Wuxian didn't pride himself on knowing Lan Wangji’s spotless character and pristine moral compass—and if Hanguang-jun’s peerless reputation hadn't been universally feared and respected—he might’ve actually started suspecting there was some messy, scandalous past between Lan Wangji and Mo Xuanyu.

Otherwise, why in the world was he putting up with this level of nonsense?!

After walking a short stretch, Wei Wuxian glanced over his shoulder. Lan Wangji was standing right where he'd left him, watching him from a distance.

Wei Wuxian’s pace instinctively slowed.

For some reason, a quiet instinct nudged at his chest, telling him that walking so fast—and leaving Lan Wangji stranded behind like that—was a bad idea.

Right then, a loud bark cut through the market chatter: "The Yiling Laozu! Five copper coins for one, ten coins for three!"

Wei Wuxian paused. "Who?!"

He wheeled around to see who on earth was putting a price tag on his head, only to find the very same shady peddler from a moment ago. Having stashed away the cheap cosmetics, he was now brandishing a thick stack of prints featuring monstrous, scowling faces that could give door gods a run for their money.

"Five for one, ten for three!" the peddler barked, voice rattling like a bronze bell. "At this price, you can't lose! Three is the charm, folks: one for the front gate, one for the parlor, and the last right above your bedpost! Choked with malice and dripping with evil—fight fire with fire, poison against poison! I guarantee no foul demon or spiteful ghoul will dare come within ten feet!"

Wei Wuxian marched over. "Talk about talking out of your ass! If they're that miraculous, why are you hawking them for five miserable coppers a pop?!"

The vendor scowled. "You again? Buy or walk, kid. If you're itching to throw down fifty coins a sheet, I won't stop you."

Wei Wuxian flipped through the stack of "Yiling Laozu Warding Prints," utterly revolted by the blue-skinned, fanged, vein-popping brute scowling back at him from the paper.

He had to defend his honor. "Wei Wuxian was a celebrated beauty, famous far and wide! What is this monstrosity supposed to be?! If you haven't seen the man in the flesh, don't butcher his face—you're misleading the youth!"

Before the peddler could fire back, Wei Wuxian caught the whisper of a draft behind him and side-stepped on pure reflex.

He cleared the strike cleanly, but the poor peddler caught the brunt of it. Sent tumbling into the street, he crashed straight into a neighboring vendor's pinwheel cart, sending paper toys scattering across the dirt in a chaotic scramble. The peddler opened his mouth to unleash a volley of curses, but seeing the attacker—a young master draped in glittering gold silk, dripping with untouchable wealth—his courage withered halfway. Then his eyes landed on the sprawling white Sparks-Amidst-Snow peony embroidered across the boy's chest, and his anger evaporated completely. Still, nursing a bruised shoulder from an unprovoked strike, he whimpered, "Why... why'd you kick me?"

The youth was Jin Ling. Crossing his arms, he looked down his nose with icy disdain. "Kick you? Anyone who dares speak the name Wei Wuxian in my presence should be on their knees thanking heaven I didn't slit their throat on the spot, and here you are screaming it across the market like a mad dog. You're begging for an early grave!"

Wei Wuxian hadn't expected Jin Ling to cross his path here, let alone act with such unhinged arrogance. What on earth went wrong with this kid's upbringing? Hair-trigger temper, venomous spite, completely wrapped up in his own ego... He managed to inherit every single flaw from his uncle and his father, yet didn't pick up an ounce of his mother's grace. If someone doesn't knock some sense into him, he's going to crash and burn hard down the line.

Seeing Jin Ling take two menacing steps toward the fallen vendor, Wei Wuxian cut in, "Jin Ling!"

The peddler kept his mouth shut, his eyes swimming with desperate gratitude. Jin Ling wheeled around, his lip curling into a sneer the second he spotted Wei Wuxian. "Still haven't run away? Fine by me."

Wei Wuxian offered a sunny, teasing grin. "Oh, my. I wonder who was pinned face-first in the dirt, entirely unable to get up last time? Remind me, who was that again?"

Jin Ling let out a sharp scoff, raised two fingers to his lips, and loosed a short, piercing whistle.

Wei Wuxian blinked, puzzled. But a heartbeat later, a heavy, ragged panting echoed from down the alleyway.

He snapped his head around. Rounding the corner at a dead sprint was a black-maned spiritual hound, standing half as tall as a grown man, barreling straight toward him! Panicked screams tore through the street, rising in pitch as bystanders scrambled out of the way: "Mad dog! Run, it's gonna bite!"

Wei Wuxian went paper-white, spun on his heel, and bolted for dear life.

To his eternal mortification, the invincible Yiling Laozu—a man who once commanded legions of the dead—was completely, utterly terrified of dogs. He couldn't help it. Back before Jiang Fengmian had pulled him off the streets, he’d spent his earliest years roaming the gutters as a feral stray, fighting snarling mutts for scraps of garbage. After taking too many vicious bites and getting hunted through frozen alleys, he’d developed a bone-deep phobia of canines big and small, a weakness Jiang Cheng had mocked relentlessly. It was a humiliating secret, and even if he told people, nobody would ever believe the terrifying Grandmaster of Demonic Cultivation was scared of a puppy, so the rumor had never spread.

Driven half out of his wits by raw terror, Wei Wuxian caught sight of a tall, snow-white silhouette standing motionless up ahead. Without a second thought, he let out a bloodcurdling shriek: "Lan Zhan, save me!"

Jin Ling sprinted into view just in time to see Lan Wangji, his face dropping in raw dismay. Why is this lunatic glued to him again?!

Lan Wangji was known for his cold, uncompromising severity. Even senior cultivators of his own generation felt a chill down their spines in his presence, let alone juniors. To these kids, his intimidating aura was ten times worse than Lan Qiren’s ever was. The spiritual hound had undergone elite training; possessing sharp animal instincts, it immediately recognized that the man in white was not someone to be trifled with. It let out a pathetic whimper, tucked its tail firmly between its hind legs, and retreated behind Jin Ling's boots.

The black-maned hound was a rare, prized breed gifted to Jin Ling by Jin Guangyao. Anyone else who heard it was a gift from Lianfang-zun would have handled it with kid gloves—unfortunately, Lan Wangji was not anyone else. He didn't care who gifted the beast or whose nephew was holding the leash; rules were rules, and offenses were punished without mercy. Caught red-handed siccing an attack dog on civilians in the middle of a public street, Jin Ling’s heart sank like a stone. I'm dead. He’s going to execute my dog, and then he’s going to skin me alive!

Before anyone could make a move, Wei Wuxian dove straight under Lan Wangji’s arm, scrambling around his back and wrapping himself around the man like a vine climbing a trellis, practically wishing he could scramble up his shoulders and vault straight into the clouds. Clutched in that desperate, full-body death grip, Lan Wangji froze completely solid.

Seizing the distraction, Jin Ling blew two frantic whistles, wheeled around, and sprinted away with his hound, beating a hasty, undignified retreat.

Over by the wreckage of the pinwheel stall, the peddler dragged himself to his feet, clutching his chest in lingering terror. "The moral decay of this generation! These young masters from the great clans really think they own the world! Simply outrageous!"

Hearing the barking fade into the distance, Wei Wuxian finally detached himself from Lan Wangji’s back. Smoothing his robes, he clasped his hands behind his back with practiced nonchalance. "Indeed. Morals are in the gutter, and virtue is dead."

Seeing Wei Wuxian as his savior, the peddler nodded fervently. In a rush of gratitude, he shoved the stack of warding prints into Wei Wuxian’s hands like a hot potato. "Brother, thank you for stepping in! Take these as a token of my thanks. If you mark them down to three coppers a sheet, you can easily walk away with three hundred coins!"

Lan Wangji cast a quiet glance at the fanged brute depicted on the paper, offering no comment.

Watching his market value drop in real time, Wei Wuxian didn't know whether to laugh or cry. "You call this a thank-you gift? If you really want to show some gratitude, hire a real artist to fix my damn face! ...Wait, hold on, don't pack up yet. I need to ask you something. Working this beat all day, have you caught wind of anything strange around here lately? Any bizarre incidents?"

The peddler puffed out his chest. "Strange occurrences? You're asking the right man! I've been running stalls here for years—folks call me the Know-It-All of Qinghe. What kind of strange are we talking about?"

Wei Wuxian hummed. "Say... demonic hauntings, severed limbs, wholesale massacres—that sort of thing."

"Nothing like that in town," the peddler said, shaking his head. "Though if you head about five or six li down that way, there's a mountain ridge called Xinglu Ridge. If you value your neck, steer clear of it."

Wei Wuxian’s brow rose. "Why's that?"

The peddler lowered his voice to a conspiratorial whisper. "Xinglu Ridge has another name around these parts: folks call it the 'Man-Eating Ridge.' What do you think?"
